name: Rice
modern_distribution: Global — staple for over half of world population
description: First domesticated along the Yangtze; spread to Southeast Asia, India, then globally via trade and colonialism

name: Wheat
modern_distribution: Global — primary grain in temperate regions
description: Among the earliest domesticated crops; foundation of bread-making cultures worldwide

name: Maize (Corn)
modern_distribution: Global after 1492 — major staple in Americas, Africa, and Asia
description: Domesticated from teosinte by Mesoamerican peoples; transformed global agriculture after Columbian Exchange

name: Potato
modern_distribution: Global — fourth most important food crop
description: Domesticated at high altitudes in the Andes; became essential in European diets after 16th century

name: Tomato
modern_distribution: Global — essential in Mediterranean and Latin American cuisines
description: Domesticated in Mesoamerica; initially feared as poisonous in Europe before becoming foundational to Italian cuisine

name: Chili Pepper
modern_distribution: Global — adopted across tropical and subtropical regions
description: One of the oldest cultivated plants in the Americas; revolutionized cuisines across Asia and Africa after 1500

name: Black Pepper
modern_distribution: Global — most traded spice worldwide
description: Called "black gold" in antiquity; drove the spice trade and European Age of Exploration

name: Cinnamon
modern_distribution: Global — widely used in both sweet and savory dishes
description: One of the earliest traded spices; prized in ancient Egypt, Rome, and medieval Europe

name: Soybean
modern_distribution: Global — major protein source and oil crop
description: Foundation of East Asian fermented foods (soy sauce, tofu, miso, tempeh)

name: Sugarcane
modern_distribution: Tropical regions globally — largest crop by production quantity
description: Spread from Oceania to India, then Arab world, then Americas via colonial plantations

name: Olive
modern_distribution: Mediterranean basin, California, South America, Australia
description: Foundation of Mediterranean diet; olive oil central to cooking, preservation, and culture

name: Garlic
modern_distribution: Global — used in virtually every cuisine
description: One of the most widely used flavoring ingredients; valued medicinally for millennia

name: Onion
modern_distribution: Global — foundational aromatic in most cuisines
description: Among the oldest cultivated vegetables; essential base ingredient across world cuisines

name: Ginger
modern_distribution: Tropical and subtropical regions globally
description: Ancient medicinal and culinary spice; spread via maritime trade to Middle East and Europe

name: Turmeric
modern_distribution: South and Southeast Asia, increasingly global
description: Sacred spice in Hindu culture; foundation of curry powders; prized for color and flavor

name: Cumin
modern_distribution: Global — essential in Middle Eastern, South Asian, and Latin American cuisines
description: One of the most used spices worldwide; mentioned in the Bible and ancient Egyptian texts

name: Coriander
modern_distribution: Global — both seeds and leaves used extensively
description: One of the oldest known herbs; found in Tutankhamun's tomb; both seeds and fresh leaves used

name: Coffee
modern_distribution: Tropical belt globally — second most traded commodity after petroleum
description: Discovered in Ethiopian highlands; spread via Yemen and Ottoman Empire to become global beverage

name: Tea
modern_distribution: Global — most consumed beverage after water
description: Cultivated for millennia in China; tea culture spread to Japan, then globally via British colonialism

name: Cacao
modern_distribution: Tropical regions globally; processed worldwide
description: Sacred drink of Maya and Aztec; transformed into modern chocolate in Europe

name: Vanilla
modern_distribution: Madagascar, Tahiti, Mexico, Indonesia
description: World's most expensive spice after saffron; pollinated by hand outside Mexico

name: Coconut
modern_distribution: Tropical coastlines worldwide
description: Tree of life — every part used; spread across Pacific by Austronesian voyagers

name: Sesame
modern_distribution: Tropical and subtropical regions globally
description: One of the oldest oilseed crops; "open sesame" reflects its cultural significance

name: Lemon
modern_distribution: Mediterranean, subtropical, and tropical regions globally
description: Spread via Arab traders to Mediterranean; essential in both Eastern and Western cuisines

name: Banana
modern_distribution: Tropical regions globally — fourth largest fruit crop
description: Domesticated in New Guinea; spread to India, Africa, then Americas via Portuguese

name: Mango
modern_distribution: Tropical regions globally — "king of fruits"
description: Sacred in Hinduism and Buddhism; spread to Southeast Asia, Africa, then Americas

name: Chickpea
modern_distribution: Mediterranean, South Asia, globally expanding
description: Foundation of hummus and falafel; one of the earliest cultivated legumes

name: Lentil
modern_distribution: South Asia, Middle East, North Africa, globally expanding
description: One of the oldest cultivated pulses; staple protein source across many cultures

name: Eggplant
modern_distribution: Global — major vegetable in Mediterranean, South Asian, and East Asian cuisines
description: Spread from India to Persia, then Arab world, and finally to Mediterranean Europe

name: Cardamom
modern_distribution: South Asia, Middle East, Scandinavia, Guatemala
description: Queen of Spices; third most expensive spice; used in chai, coffee, and Scandinavian baking

name: Saffron
modern_distribution: Iran, India, Spain, Morocco
description: World's most expensive spice by weight; requires 150,000 flowers per kilogram

name: Nutmeg
modern_distribution: Indonesia, Grenada, India
description: Wars were fought over Banda Islands' nutmeg monopoly; drove European colonialism in Southeast Asia

name: Clove
modern_distribution: Indonesia, Madagascar, Tanzania, Sri Lanka
description: Extremely valuable spice monopolized by successive colonial powers

name: Star Anise
modern_distribution: China, Vietnam, Southeast Asia
description: Key ingredient in Chinese five-spice; essential in Vietnamese pho broth

name: Tamarind
modern_distribution: Tropical regions globally
description: Spread from Africa to India where it became essential; used in pad thai, chutneys, and Latin American drinks

name: Peanut
modern_distribution: Global — major protein and oil crop in tropical regions
description: Spread from South America to Africa and Asia via Portuguese traders; transformed Asian cuisines

name: Cassava
modern_distribution: Tropical regions globally — staple for 800+ million people
description: Spread from Amazon to Africa and Asia; critical food security crop in tropical developing nations

name: Sweet Potato
modern_distribution: Global — especially important in East Asia and Africa
description: Reached Polynesia before European contact; major crop in China, Japan, and Africa

name: Avocado
modern_distribution: Americas, Mediterranean, Southeast Asia, expanding globally
description: Sacred fruit of the Aztecs; global popularity surged in late 20th century

name: Fig
modern_distribution: Mediterranean, California, Middle East
description: Possibly the earliest cultivated fruit; predates grain agriculture

name: Date Palm
modern_distribution: Middle East, North Africa, California
description: Tree of Life in Mesopotamian culture; staple food of desert civilizations

name: Mustard
modern_distribution: Global — both seeds and prepared condiments
description: Used in ancient Rome and India; essential condiment in both European and Asian cuisines

name: Fennel
modern_distribution: Mediterranean, India, China, Americas
description: Ancient Greek Olympic athletes ate fennel for stamina; used in both sweet and savory cooking

name: Mint
modern_distribution: Global — one of the most widely distributed herbs
description: Used in teas, sauces, and garnishes across cultures; central to Moroccan tea ceremony

name: Basil
modern_distribution: Global — especially Mediterranean and Southeast Asia
description: Sacred in Hinduism (tulsi); became Italian cuisine's defining herb; Thai basil distinct variety

name: Cilantro/Coriander Leaf
modern_distribution: Global — polarizing flavor due to genetic differences in taste perception
description: Fresh leaves vs dried seeds serve distinct culinary roles; genetic basis for soap-taste controversy

name: Lamb/Sheep
modern_distribution: Global — especially Middle East, Mediterranean, Central Asia
description: Among the first domesticated animals; central to pastoral cultures and religious traditions

name: Chicken
modern_distribution: Global — most consumed meat worldwide
description: Descended from red junglefowl; spread globally; now most numerous bird on Earth

name: Cattle (Beef)
modern_distribution: Global — but taboo in Hindu cultures, restricted in others
description: Two independent domestication events; sacred in Hinduism; central to Argentine, American, and European cuisines

name: Pig (Pork)
modern_distribution: Global except Muslim and Jewish cultures — most consumed meat historically
description: Two independent domestication events; taboo in Islam and Judaism; central to Chinese and European cuisines

name: Fish Sauce
modern_distribution: Southeast Asia primarily; Roman garum revived
description: Roman garum and Southeast Asian fish sauce developed independently; umami foundation in many cuisines

name: Yogurt
modern_distribution: Global — especially Middle East, South Asia, Mediterranean
description: Likely discovered accidentally by nomadic peoples; foundation of Turkish and Indian cuisines

name: Fermented Soybean (Miso/Doenjang)
modern_distribution: East Asia primarily; expanding globally
description: Chinese jiang evolved into Japanese miso and Korean doenjang; fundamental umami source

name: Ghee
modern_distribution: South Asia, East Africa, Middle East
description: Clarified butter essential in Ayurvedic tradition; survives tropical heat without refrigeration

name: Olive Oil
modern_distribution: Mediterranean basin, expanding globally
description: Foundation of Mediterranean cooking; ancient trade commodity; symbol of peace and prosperity

name: Palm Oil
modern_distribution: Tropical regions globally — most produced vegetable oil
description: Native to West Africa; now dominated by Indonesian and Malaysian production

name: Quinoa
modern_distribution: Andes, expanding globally since 21st century
description: Sacred crop of the Inca ("mother grain"); global superfood trend since 2000s

name: Millet
modern_distribution: East Asia, South Asia, Africa
description: Multiple independent domestication events; drought-resistant staple for arid regions

name: Sorghum
modern_distribution: Africa, South Asia, Americas
description: Fifth most important cereal crop globally; staple grain of sub-Saharan Africa

name: Wasabi
modern_distribution: Japan primarily; limited cultivation elsewhere
description: Extremely difficult to cultivate; most "wasabi" outside Japan is actually horseradish with coloring
